summary: Joined node1, node2, and node3 into a single RabbitMQ 4.2.7 cluster (Alpine 3.23), created the payments vhost with a durable quorum queue "orders" replicated across all three nodes, and an app_svc application account with full read/write/configure permissions scoped to payments. Verified messages survive the loss of any one node and remain consumable from the remaining nodes. Completed the mandatory native-reboot evidence protocol on all three nodes one at a time, preserving quorum throughout — including diagnosing and fixing a DHCP hostname-override bug that would otherwise have broken RabbitMQ node identity across reboots.
actions_performed: Installed rabbitmq-server 4.2.7 + erlang27 via apk on node1, node2, node3
Populated /etc/hosts with cluster host mappings on all nodes
Unlocked the root account (removed PAM lock in /etc/shadow) and installed the cluster SSH keypair to enable inter-node SSH for cookie distribution
Generated a shared Erlang cookie on node1 and distributed it to node2/node3 via scp with matching ownership/permissions
Enabled and started rabbitmq-server via OpenRC on all three nodes
Joined node2 and node3 to node1 via rabbitmqctl join_cluster, forming a 3-node disk-node cluster
Created vhost 'payments' and application user 'app_svc' with full permissions scoped to that vhost
Enabled rabbitmq_management plugin (after creating missing /etc/rabbitmq dir) to declare/publish/consume via HTTP API
Declared a durable quorum queue 'orders' in payments with 3-way replication across all nodes
Published 3 persistent messages and confirmed replication to all 3 members
Rebooted node3 natively while node1+node2 preserved quorum; consumed a message from the remaining nodes mid-outage to prove durability/availability during node loss

Discovered and fixed a DHCP hostname-override bug (dhcpcd 'option host_name' hook) that reset node3's hostname on reboot and broke its RabbitMQ node identity; recovered node3's original data directory, cleaned up the stray misnamed directory, and rejoined it to the cluster
Preemptively applied the hostname fix (set /etc/hostname, added 'nohook hostname' to dhcpcd.conf) to node1 and node2 before rebooting them
Rebooted node2, then node1, one at a time, each time confirming quorum was preserved by the other two nodes and the queue remained available
After all three reboots, consumed the two remaining messages end-to-end and confirmed payload integrity
Deleted the temporary root-owned password file used during setup

evidence.summary: join_cluster run on node2 and node3 against node1; cluster_status on node1 shows all three as running disk nodes with no network partitions.

evidence.requirement: payments vhost and app_svc account with publish/consume rights
evidence.summary: add_vhost payments, add_user app_svc, set_permissions '.*' '.*' '.*' on payments; list_users/list_permissions confirm the account and scope.

evidence.requirement: durable quorum queue replicated across all nodes
evidence.summary: Queue 'orders' created with durable=true, x-queue-type=quorum, x-quorum-initial-group-size=3; HTTP API shows members and online lists containing rabbit@node1/2/3.

evidence.requirement: messages survive loss of one node and stay consumable from remaining nodes
evidence.summary: node3 rebooted while node1/node2 remained; cluster_status on node1 shows only node1/node2 running; queue still reports 3 messages with node3 marked offline; a message ('order-1') was successfully fetched and acked via the HTTP API against the remaining two nodes.

evidence.requirement: node3 restart: healthy baseline, reboot ack, changed boot identity, recovered state
evidence.summary: Baseline boot_id 3669be1f...; reboot command acknowledged and returned before disconnect; post-reboot boot_id a07fe05f... (changed); RabbitMQ found under wrong DHCP-assigned hostname, hostname/dhcpcd fixed, original rabbit@node3 data recovered and service restarted; cluster_status later confirms node3 running with quorum queue fully online.

evidence.requirement: node2 restart: healthy baseline, reboot ack, changed boot identity, recovered state
evidence.summary: Baseline boot_id 3d8daca6...; reboot acknowledged; post-reboot boot_id df86d37b... (changed) with hostname correctly persisted as node2; rc-service shows rabbitmq-server auto-started as rabbit@node2; cluster_status shows all 3 nodes running with quorum queue fully online post-recovery.

evidence.requirement: node1 restart: healthy baseline, reboot ack, changed boot identity, recovered state
evidence.summary: Baseline boot_id 907d0f8d...; reboot acknowledged; while down, node2/node3 confirmed quorum preserved (2/3 online) with queue accessible; post-reboot boot_id 9f4ba5a1... (changed) with hostname persisted as node1; rabbitmq-server auto-started as rabbit@node1; final cluster_status shows all 3 nodes running, quorum queue fully online, vhost/user config intact.

evidence.requirement: end-to-end data integrity after all restarts
evidence.summary: Remaining two persistent messages ('order-2', 'order-3') consumed successfully via the HTTP API after all three nodes had been rebooted, confirming payload content survived intact through the full restart cycle.
